transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM), Alex Turner (Citrine CTO), Sofia Ramos (Citrine Platform Eng), Priya Shah (Citrine Data Privacy)

Summary (auto): QBR focused on usage/costs, recent production retries, Dedicated sizing options and PII handling/retention. Next steps agreed.

00:00 Jordan Lee: All right, uh, good afternoon everyone. Thanks for joining the QBR. I see we have Alex, Sofia and Priya from Citrine, can you hear me okay?
00:06 Alex Turner: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Jordan. Appreciate you carving out time.
00:10 Maya Patel: Hi team, Maya here from Redwood CS, I'll run health metrics with you and then we'll hand off to Jordan for roadmap and pricing.
00:18 Sofia Ramos: Hi, quick heads up
Sofia on my side, I might dip out around the 40 minute mark for another sync, but I'll stay through the core parts.

02:05 Maya Patel: Okay cool, starting with usage. Over the last quarter we saw active requests up 3.4x month-over-month driven by the triage assistant and search summarization workloads. Your monthly token volume at March end was ~1.8 billion tokens, and cost, as you know, scaled with model mix
about 62% of spend is on gpt-compatible-large-1 and 28% on smaller embedding endpoints.
02:35 Priya Shah: Sorry real quick, when you say 'gpt-compatible-large-1', is that the Redwood hosted variant or our dedicated cluster?
02:42 Jordan Lee: That's hosted. For Dedicated yeah we'd recommend a different selection
more quantized/FP16 variants to reduce unit costs.

04:12 Maya Patel: On cost breakdown, the big drivers were gen tokens for triage (45% of gen spend), and embeddings used for vector search increased due to expanded document ingestion. We attached a cost per 1k tokens chart in the deck  (link: shorturl.com/redwood-costs)
04:32 Alex Turner: The rising embeddings cost is something we flagged. We're also seeing higher tail latency spikes during 11am-1pm PST, which hits our SLAs.

06:00 Jordan Lee: Yeah about those spikes
SE noted two incidents last month where preemptible nodes caused KV cache cold starts. We put a mitigation in place: a pre-warm policy and cache affinity, which reduced incidents by ~70% in the second half of the month.
06:20 Sofia Ramos: I recall the incident, we saw 600ms added P99 for a few minutes. The mitigation helped but we'd like predictability. This ties into Dedicated discussion.

08:15 Jordan Lee: Right. For Dedicated sizing, we proposed a 4-GPU pool with autoscale to 6 for bursts, that gives you consistent tail latency under our target. It's in the pricing spreadsheet we shared last week. The main tradeoff is commit vs. burst costs.
08:40 Alex Turner: Can you run through the burst policy? Our infra team is sensitive to overcommit; they want to understand billing when we exceed reserved capacity.
08:55 Jordan Lee: Sure. The playbook: reserved capacity covers baseline throughput at a committed rate; bursts are billed at a higher per-hour rate but you only pay when used. We can also set a hard cap to prevent runaway costs, and automatic fallback to hosted endpoints if Dedicated capacity is exhausted
so application stays up.

11:30 Priya Shah: On the privacy front, our legal requires KMS-backed key management and 90-day data retention for short lived logs. We're also exploring an on-prem pilot for PHI traffic. What's Redwood's path for Private/on-prem?
11:48 Maya Patel: We're doing Private deployments now  
customer-managed control plane in your VPC or a full on-prem package. For PHI we recommend on-prem or VPC with HSM for keys. We have SOC2 Type II and ISO docs
I'll share the package link after this call.
12:10 Priya Shah: Great. Also need audit logs for model access with SSO integration (SAML). Can you confirm RBAC + fine-grained audit event retention?
12:20 Jordan Lee: Yes, RBAC is configurable and audit logs can be pushed to your logging endpoint with configurable retention windows. We'll include exact event schema in the security pack.

14:00 Sofia Ramos: A couple technical asks from platform: 1) Does the Dedicated offering support mixed-precision quantization? 2) Can we pin model versions per route so experimental prompts won't affect production?
14:18 Jordan Lee: Yes to both, Dedicated supports int8/4-bit quantized variants and you can pin model versions per route; rollouts can be canary/A-B or automatic fallback.

16:05 Maya Patel: Quick health numbers
uptime was 99.95% this quarter, incident MTTD down to 8 minutes, MTR about 23 minutes average. We flagged two regressed evals last month (prompt set A) where rouge scores dropped ~3 points; SE is tracking.
16:30 Alex Turner: About those evals
was that due to a model rollout or infra change?
16:36 Jordan Lee: That was a model variant swap on embeddings; we caught it via evals and rolled back within the hour. Going forward we're proposing pre-rollout regression gates for critical prompts.

19:00 Alex Turner: On the roadmap items
what's the timeline for the Private pilot and the Dedicated autoscaler improvements?
19:10 Jordan Lee: Private pilot readiness is Q2 end
ops can start planning the network and KMS integration now. Autoscaler improvements (better burst smoothing) are slated for mid-Q3. We'll prioritize options that help P99 stability.

22:45 Sofia Ramos: For the on-prem pilot, our network team will need a checklist. Can you send a minimal port list and bootstrap steps?
22:54 Maya Patel: Yes we'll send a deployment checklist and a playbook for network/firewall rules. Also sending the Dedicated sizing template.

25:30 Alex Turner: A few concerns
cost predictability is key for finance. Could we get a modeled cost projection for both hosted vs Dedicated (3-month and 12-month) with current traffic trends?
25:45 Jordan Lee: Yep we'll provide a modeled projection with sensitivity to 2x and 4x traffic. That's part of the pricing deliverable.

28:12 Priya Shah: SLA question
what do we have for latency and availability credits? Do we get compensation if P99 exceeds target regularly?
28:25 Jordan Lee: For Dedicated customers we have SLA credits tied to uptime. For tail latency we offer SLO-based runbooks and can set custom SLOs as part of the enterprise contract; credits for latency are negotiable and tied to defined measurement windows.

31:40 Sofia Ramos: Also, can we schedule a benchmark run? We'd like Redwood to run the triage assistant against our top 10 prompts to measure P50/P95/P99 with our data.
31:52 Jordan Lee: Absolutely
if you can share the prompt set and a sampling of documents we'll run a benchmark on both Hosted and Dedicated and share results.

34:10 Alex Turner: One more thing
security asks around FedRAMP-ish controls; we don't need FedRAMP itself but a gap analysis would be helpful for our risk team.
34:20 Maya Patel: We can provide a controls matrix mapping Redwood capabilities to common frameworks and highlight gaps. That will be in the security packet.

36:05 Jordan Lee: Ok let's recap. Action items: Jordan to send Dedicated pricing + sizing + cost model by 2026-04-16; Maya to send security pack and deployment checklist by 2026-04-15; Alex to share top 10 prompts and P99 targets by 2026-04-19; schedule Dedicated playbook walkthrough (Maya to own). Any additions?
36:35 Alex Turner: That covers it. Quick Q
what's the recommended quantization profile for triage assistant latency/cost tradeoff?
36:45 Jordan Lee: For triage we'd recommend int8 with KV cache affinity; that yields ~30-40% cost savings with <5% quality delta in our evals.

38:00 Priya Shah: Noted. One last privacy item
retention of user utterances for audit; can we set separate retention for raw logs and derived embeddings?
38:12 Maya Patel: Yes, retention policies can be decoupled; raw logs can be short-lived and embeddings persisted if you want, or vice versa per your policy.

41:00 Sofia Ramos: Sorry I'm late back
just saw calendar update. Any open blockers from our side?
41:06 Alex Turner: Only waiting on pricing and the benchmark run. We'll get the prompts to you today.

44:00 Jordan Lee: Great. Thanks everyone for the time. We'll follow up with the deliverables and calendar invites. Enjoy the rest of your day.
44:08 Alex Turner: Thanks Jordan, thanks Maya. Appreciate it.
44:12 Maya Patel: Thanks all.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions: 'Red wood' vs Redwood, 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed 'K V cache', 'gpt-compatible-large-1' may be rendered differently in deck. Some timestamps approximate.
